description: Small team interested in all things space
summary: We developed Marscope, an interactive 2D/3D Mars exploration platform, designed to make it simple and easy for martian astronauts to carry out missions.It works by using a multi terrain visualization system drawing directly from nasa data to show terrain in multiple ways useful to astronauts. We acknowledge that all NASA space missions ultimately have the same goal of advancing science, which is why we integrate a science aware route planning that increases the possibility that the route croses through locations of scientific interest.It helps astronauts by catering to a wide variety of missions. In the future features like the HUD view that could be displayed on astronauts helmets; dynamic obstacle detectiction and replanning;mission summaries and reports ;and the fact that it uses multiple sources of official NASA data and turns it into actionable advice will be very important to scientists on Mars.
details: The underlying framework that Marscope uses for routing is a multi objective algorithm combining Djikstra and A* pathfinding to locate the most efficient route between two points that the astronaut specifies on the map, and LPA* for incremental planning when an obstacle is observed. The data it needs to do this is sourced from NASA PDS , ODE and Mars Trek data sources.The astronauts can adjust multiple variables, such as equipment mass,energy budget, maximum slope and so on. These factors are automatically integrated into the route, and enables it to display this in a concise form on astronaut helmet head up display for seamless AR visualization.A unique feature we have is that our program can load in scientifically significant areas and route the user safely through this path, enabling greater scientific discovery.Dynamic routing that identifies obstacles and replans can be used in assistance with auto generated mission reports/summaries for official nasa spacewalks. Furthermore, the astronaut can pick and choose between 3 generated routes, each with its own benefits and downsides stated trasparently, along with other data such as a cross section of the path and data such as distance.
